pr_title: Rework docs for the `size` of `terms` agg
pr_body:
The `terms` agg picks the top `size` terms in a single scatter/gather
pass across all the shards. For the default `order` and if you `order`
by `_key` this works quite well. Some errors creep in, but it's fairly
easy to point to them and understand them. But ordering by doc count
ascending is like inviting the error vampire into your agg. It's super
easy to get inaccurate results. This updates the docs to be more stark
about it.

Closes #72684
pr_comments: @jrodewig I merged all of your suggestions and reworked one section a little. I did a fair bit of renaming `bucket` to `term` but we can't really do that everywhere. `bucket` appears in the api and is a general concept in aggs land that sort of can't be ignored.

issue_context.title: Slightly more accurate `terms` sorting on sub-aggs
issue_context.body: Right now we default the `shard_size` to `1.5*size+10` in `terms` in an effort to keep the doc count errors lower. When you sort the terms by something other than doc_count descending the error is unbounded. But larger `shard_size` will lead to more accurate results because we ship more data back to the coordinating node. Maybe we should bump the `shard_size` if you are sorting on anything other than doc_count descending to get you more accurate results by default. Sure, it'll be slower, but it's the price you pay for a little more accuracy. And the performance when sorting by the default won't change.
comments:
A few of us go to talking about this and figured out we don't really know how often we get into this state. We [document](https://www.elastic.co/guide/en/elasticsearch/reference/current/search-aggregations-bucket-terms-aggregation.html#terms-agg-doc-count-error) that this sort of thing can be an error. We're not super clear about the side effects here. I think we use kind of dense language. I think we can improve that.

Anyway! It'd be useful to collect a counter of how often this happens. I'm not sure it's worth the effort right now. We're kind of swamped and we're not sure that we'd really do with the counter.

We don't have a good way to fix this. The errors are still unbounded. Even if we bump the shard_size. It'd help. Some. But we don't know how much and it'd absolutely come with performance changes. And, even better, you can do this yourself. Just set the `shard_size` higher.

So! I'm going to convert this into a docs issue and just update those docs and leave the rest as it.
